*Reasoning in my own voice:*

Aiya, 55 years I've been on this land. My wife and I, just the two of us now — the children went to the city years ago, they send money sometimes. 3 mu isn't much but it's what we have. We eat from it and sell a little.

**Wheat.** I plant after the cold dew, around when the weather turns proper cold — that's mid October. I keep some seed back from last year's harvest, save money that way, my father did the same. Before sowing, I pay the neighbor's boy to plow with his tractor, 50 yuan a mu — my back won't do it anymore. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer across the whole 3 mu before planting, that's how I always do it. In spring when the wheat turns green again, I carry a bag of urea out and spread it by hand, maybe half a bag each mu. Water the field before winter once, then after green-up twice more when the ground cracks. Electricity for the pump isn't cheap, so I don't water unless I have to. Some years I spray once for the grass in the field. Wheat usually gives me seven or eight bags per mu at harvest — about 350 kg. Not like the young ones with their new seed, but enough.

**Maize.** Soon as wheat is off the field in June, no time to waste — the neighbor comes with his little planter the same week, we put the maize straight in. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town, can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. One bag of compound at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I put urea again. If it doesn't rain after planting I run the well once to get the seedlings up. Harvest around Mid-Autumn. Maize does a little better than wheat — maybe 400 kg a mu in a good year.

I don't spray much. Pesticide costs money, and my eyes aren't good for mixing chemicals. I walk the field, pull weeds by hand when I can, spray only if the bugs are bad.
